title: Who pays for Israel’s nuclear dominance?
author: Jamal Kanj
description: The war against Iran is exacting a growing price from Americans, while Washington shields Israel’s nuclear dominance from scrutiny.

title: How much higher can oil prices go?
author: Joshua Busby and Greg Pollock
description: As conflict in Iran drags on, dwindling oil supplies and exhausted safeguards could push energy costs higher.

title: What kind of world order is emerging?
author: Mizan R Khan
description: The emerging world order reflects China’s rise, resurgent nationalism, weakening multilateralism, technological disruption and climate change in an increasingly multipolar world.

title: Prelude to an order for genocide
author: Rehman Sobhan
description: AS President Yahya flew out of Dacca on the night of March 25 he took with him the last hopes of a united Pakistan. For the final two days he had been holed up in the Dacca cantonment with the junta of generals who rule Pakistan, putting the finishing touches to Operation Genocide.

title: The untold history of why Khaleda Zia entered politics
author: Mahfuz Ullah
description: Why did Khaleda Zia, a typical housewife who had become widow at a critical age in terms of Bangladesh's culture, join politics?

title: Do great leaders make history, or does history make them?
author: Maleeha Lodhi
description: Exceptional leaders only change history’s trajectory when favourable contextual, economic, and social conditions enable their decisive impact.

title: Poison and cremation: A forensic history of colonial Bengal
author: Mitra Sharafi
description: Forensic experts in colonial Bengal navigated planted poisons, cremation challenges, and racial biases to prevent wrongful convictions.

title: Partition, Bor Porong and the Chakmas’ unfinished struggle for belonging
author: Anita Mondal
description: Explore the historical trauma of the Chakma people, from the 1947 Partition and the Kaptai Dam displacement to their ongoing struggle for citizenship in India.

title: The young radicals who challenged 19th-century Bengal
author: Priyam Paul
description: Professor Rosinka Chaudhuri discusses her new book on the Young Bengal group, exploring their radical legacy, areligious modernity, and impact on Indian thought.

title: More men are cooking. But is patriarchy leaving the kitchen?
author: Khairul Hassan Jahin
description: As more men in urban Dhaka enter the kitchen, we explore if this shift truly challenges traditional gender roles or if domestic labour remains a woman's burden.

title: Everyday secularism and the Bangladesh we rarely talk about
author: Anas Ansar
description: Beyond political debates, a quieter, resilient form of secularism thrives in Bangladesh. Discover how ordinary people preserve pluralism through everyday habits.

title: Reading Sarat Chandra at 150, with empathy
author: Madhurima Sen
description: At 150, Sarat Chandra’s enduring empathy invites us to confront his literary limitations while rediscovering the power of compassion.

title: Who really owned Britain’s royal jewels?
author: F.S. Aijazuddin
description: Queen Camilla enthusiastically wears British Crown jewels, illustrating how inherited royal family jewellery continually symbolises monarchical prestige.

title: The 25,000-year history of betel nut chewing
author: Adam Brumm, Carney D. Matheson, Fakhri, Melandri Vlok & Roger Papke
description: Scientists have traced betel nut chewing to Ice Age Sulawesi, revealing a 25,000-year-old history of habitual psychoactive drug use.

title: The world map we know is distorted. Why does it matter?
author: Derek H. Alderman and Jack Swab
description: The UN has endorsed the Equal Earth projection to provide a more accurate view of landmasses. Experts explain why this matters for global perception.

title: Bengal and the coming of Islam: A story of soil and spirit
author: Syed Ali Nadeem Rezavi
description: Islam’s arrival in Bengal was no single event, but a centuries-long story of conquest, cultivation, cultural exchange and spiritual transformation.

title: Xuanzang’s travels to Bengal and beyond : The man, the pilgrim and the Monkey King
author: Zarif Faiaz
description: Discover the journey of Xuanzang, the Chinese monk who documented ancient Bengal, Mahasthangarh, and the intellectual landscape of the 7th century.

title: Professor Anisur Rahman: The economist who put people at the centre
author: Selim Jahan
description: Remembering Professor Anisur Rahman, the legendary economist and social thinker who shaped Bangladesh's economic thought. A personal tribute by Dr. Selim Jahan.

title: APO 433: Dhaka’s forgotten post office of World War II
author: Ystiaque Ahmed
description: Discover the hidden history of APO 433, the US military post office that connected Dhaka to the world during the Second World War. Read the full story.

title: Dadabhai Naoroji: The man who exposed the economics of British colonialism
author: Priyam Paul
description: Dadabhai Naoroji exposed British colonialism’s economic exploitation, linking India’s poverty to political power and making swaraj a nationalist imperative.

title: The extraordinary journey of Atish Dipankar Srigyan
author: Dipen Bhattacharya
description: Explore the life and legacy of Atish Dipankar Srigyan, the legendary Buddhist scholar from Bikrampur who shaped Tibetan Buddhism. A deep dive into history.

title: Forgotten story of Jeanette Van Tassel, the American woman who flew over Dhaka in 1892
author: Fahima Kaniz Lava
description: Jeanette Van Tassel was a 24 year old American aeronaut whose balloon ascent over Dhaka's Buriganga River in 1892 was meant to dazzle a city. Instead, it ended in her death after a rescue attempt went tragically wrong, leaving her buried in an unmarked grave in Old Dhaka. More than a century later, a researcher's chance discovery brought her remarkable story back to light.

title: A personal essay
author: Sunita Chowdhurie
description: Beyond 1947 is a personal essay by Sunita Chowdhurie about the two grandmothers who shaped her, women who never called it Independence, only Partition. Through memory, food, and quiet endurance, it traces what was lost and rebuilt when a border cut through Bengal.

title: A global quest in search of a nation
author: Rochona Majumdar
description: Abul Mansur Ahmad’s vision of Bengali Muslim identity went beyond the boundaries of East Pakistan, connecting questions of language, culture, sovereignty and autonomy to wider global histories of decolonisation.

title: Chand Bibi and the forgotten history of Muslim women’s political resistance
author: Miftahul Jannat
description: In this interview with The Daily Star, historian Sarah Waheed, author of Chand Bibi: The Lives and Legends of a Warrior Queen, traces how oral legend, court chronicles and Deccani paintings kept her memory alive, and what her story reveals about the erased political power of Muslim women across South Asia.

title: Women’s voices in Nazrul’s Dhumketu
author: Niaz Zaman
description: Nazrul’s *Dhumketu* is remembered for rebellion, but its pages also gave women writers a powerful voice for freedom.

title: How Milad-un-Nabi shaped Muslim cultural life in colonial Bengal
author: Mohammad Abu Sayed
description: Explore how Milad-un-Nabi celebrations in schools helped foster a distinct cultural identity among the Muslim middle class in colonial Bengal.
